name: יִזְרְעֶאל
summary: Jezreel is chiefly a place, the city of Ahab's palace and Naboth's vineyard and the valley below it; two men bear the name: Hosea's firstborn son by Gomer, and a man of Judah among the sons of the father of Etam (1Ch 4:3). The name is the imperfect of זָרַע “sow” with אֵל “God”: “God sows”, or “may God sow”, as Israel and Ishmael are formed. Hosea's son is named for the place, for Yahweh will visit the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu (Hos 1:4–5); but the prophet then turns the name to its meaning: “great is the day of Jezreel” when Judah and Israel are gathered under one head, the earth answers grain, wine and oil, “and they shall answer Jezreel, and I will sow her for myself in the land” (Hos 2:2, 24–25), the promise Paul quotes of the nations called to be God's people (Rom 9:25).

evidence.note: “Call his name יִזְרְעֶאל, for yet a little while and I will visit the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu.”
“I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.”
Judah and Israel gathered under one head, “for great is the day of Jezreel”.
“The earth shall answer the grain and the new wine and the oil, and they shall answer יִזְרְעֶאל; and I will sow her (וּזְרַעְתִּיהָ) for myself in the land”: the name read by its verb.
Hos 2:25 quoted: “I will call them my people which were not my people.”
“These were the father of Etam: Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash.”
The place: “Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard which was in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab.”
The same verb of a people: “I will sow them among the peoples … and they shall live.”

note: Takes g.cl.af (36 tokens, nearly all the place: Jos 15:56 in Judah, Jos 19:18 in Issachar, the city and valley of 1Ki 18–21, 2Ki 8–10, Hos 1:5) and the gentilic יִזְרְעֵאלִי, יִזְרְעֵאלִית (g.cl.ag, 13 tokens: Naboth the Jezreelite, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess), which TIPNR lists as forms of the place Jezreel@Jos.19.18; only the two men are tagged, the places being place records. Hos 1:4 has the name twice, once the son and once the place. The analysis “God sows” is from the form (yiqtol of זָרַע plus אֵל, the pattern of יִשְׂרָאֵל and יִשְׁמָעֵאל), which Hos 2:24–25 plays on; no verse states it as the reason for the name.
